model.title: Temporary trade-liberalisation measures applicable to Armenian products

summary.lead: Official summary (Legislative Observatory, Decision by Parliament, 1st reading):

blocks.text: The European Parliament adopted by 583 votes to 49, with 39 abstentions, a legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on temporary trade-liberalisation measures applicable to Armenian products.
The European Parliament adopted its position at first reading, taking over the Commission's proposal.

The proposal introduces targeted trade liberalisation measures to improve Armenian producers' access to the EU market, facilitate the reorientation of trade flows, and strengthen the resilience of the Armenian economy. More broadly, it aims to deepen EU-Armenia economic relations, in line with the EU-Armenia Comprehensive and Enhanced Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
More specifically, the proposed regulation introduces trade liberalisation measures in the form of:

- the suspension of ad valorem duties similar to the suspensions envisaged by the Union’s Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus schedule with some adjustments, such as the removal of certain sensitive products and the inclusion of certain agricultural goods banned by Russia;

- the removal of ad valorem duties on eight agricultural products within the limits of applicable tariff quotas (cucumbers and gherkins, fresh and dried grapes, pears, apricots, cherries, peaches, plums, strawberries).
The trade liberalisation measures are subject to the following conditions :
- Armenia's respect for the rules of origin;
- Armenia engaging in close and effective administrative cooperation with the Union, including for the verification of evidence of origin, in order to prevent any risk of fraud;

- Armenia abstaining from introducing new duties or charges having equivalent effect or new quantitative restrictions or measures having equivalent effect, from increasing existing levels of duties or charges and from introducing any other restrictions on trade with the Union unless they are duly justified and notified to the Commission; and
- Armenia's respect for democratic principles, the rule of law, human rights and fundamental freedoms and countering the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.

In the event that Armenia fails to comply with any of those conditions, the Commission should be empowered to suspend temporarily , in whole or in part, the trade-liberalisation measures provided for in this Regulation.
The proposal also includes safeguard measures allowing the EU to suspend or reinstate tariffs if imports cause or are likely to cause serious difficulties for producers in the Union.

The European Parliament has approved, by 583 votes to 49 with 39 abstentions, a proposed regulation that would temporarily open the EU market more widely to Armenian products. Parliament adopted its position at first reading, taking over the European Commission's proposal.

The aim is to give Armenian producers better access to the EU market, make it easier for Armenia to redirect its trade, and make its economy more resilient. The measure also seeks to deepen economic ties between the EU and Armenia, in line with their Comprehensive and Enhanced Partnership Agreement.

In practice, the regulation would suspend ad valorem duties (taxes based on a product's value) on a range of Armenian goods, in a similar way to the EU's Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus, with some changes. Certain sensitive products are left out, and some farm goods that Russia has banned are included. Separately, duties would be removed on eight farm products, including cucumbers, grapes, pears, apricots, cherries, peaches, plums and strawberries, within the limits of the applicable tariff quotas.

These openings depend on several conditions. Armenia must follow the rules of origin, cooperate closely and effectively with the EU on administrative matters, including checking evidence of origin to prevent fraud, and avoid introducing new duties, charges or quantitative restrictions, or raising existing ones, unless these are properly justified and notified to the Commission. Armenia must also respect democratic principles, the rule of law, human rights and fundamental freedoms, and act against the spread of weapons of mass destruction. If Armenia fails to meet any of these conditions, the Commission could temporarily suspend the measures, in whole or in part.
The proposal also includes safeguard measures. If imports cause, or are likely to cause, serious difficulties for EU producers, the EU can suspend or reinstate tariffs.
